key_insight: In small exact simulations, fixed-angle QASPA-MaxCut achieved group-mean selection ratios of 0.955–1.000, exceeding the reported depth-one QAOA mean scores.
engineering_relevance: The study highlights how circuit design, classical candidate selection, and optimizer restart budgets jointly affect shallow quantum Max-Cut performance.
method: Encode graph edges with CX–Ry(θ)–CX blocks in a shift-phase circuit.
Score QASPA by retaining the best cut among its four leading bit strings.
Compare against depth-one QAOA expected approximation ratios with 1–10 optimization restarts.
evidence_signal: Seed-42 exact state-vector tests covered backbone-augmented random graphs at four edge probabilities and 19 custom unweighted topologies; retained finite-shot checks preserved topology-level readout.
watch_item: QASPA’s best-of-four selection score and QAOA’s expected ratio are different metrics, and small simulations do not establish hardware-scale advantage.
paper_title: QASPA-MaxCut on Unweighted Graphs: Edge Encoding and QAOA Restarts
